title: Ch 9 Test: Light – Reflection and Refraction
subject: Science
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks. Section E: case-based, 4 marks.
Use the New Cartesian Sign Convention. Show the formula, substitution and units in numericals. Draw ray diagrams neatly.

questions.q: Which of the following can make a parallel beam of light when light from a point source is incident on it?
options: Two plane mirrors at 90° to each other
questions.answer: (d) Concave mirror and convex lens (with the source placed at the focus).

questions.q: The image formed by a concave mirror is virtual, erect and larger than the object. Where is the object placed?
options: Between the pole P and F
questions.answer: (d) Between the pole P and F

questions.q: The focal length of a lens is +50 cm. Its power is:
The refractive index of glass is 1.5. The speed of light in glass is (speed of light in vacuum = 3 × 10^{8} m/s):
The mirror used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles is:
questions.answer: (a) convex. It gives an erect image and a wider field of view.

questions.q:
**Assertion (A):** The magnification produced by a convex mirror is always positive and less than 1.
**Reason (R):** A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: Define the principal focus of a concave mirror. The radius of curvature of a spherical mirror is 20 cm. What is its focal length?
questions.answer: Rays parallel to the principal axis, after reflection from a concave mirror, all meet at a point on the principal axis called the principal focus. f = R/2 = 20/2 = 10 cm.

or.q: State the two laws of refraction of light.
or.answer: (1) The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane. (2) For a given pair of media and a given colour of light, the ratio sin i / sin r is a constant (Snell's law).

questions.q: A ray of light travelling in air enters water at an angle. Does it bend towards or away from the normal? Why?
questions.answer: It bends towards the normal. Light travels more slowly in water, which is optically denser than air.

questions.q: An object 4 cm high is placed 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm.

subparts.q: Find the position of the image.
subparts.answer: u = −15 cm, f = −10 cm. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/10 + 1/15 = −1/30, so v = −30 cm. The image is 30 cm in front of the mirror.

subparts.q: Find the size and nature of the image.
subparts.answer: m = −v/u = −(−30)/(−15) = −2, so h′ = −2 × 4 = −8 cm. The image is real, inverted and magnified (8 cm tall).

questions.q: A concave lens has a focal length of 15 cm. At what distance from the lens should an object be placed so that the image is formed 10 cm from the lens? Find the magnification.
questions.answer: f = −15 cm, v = −10 cm (a concave lens forms a virtual image on the same side). 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, so 1/u = 1/v − 1/f = −1/10 + 1/15 = −1/30, and u = −30 cm. The object is 30 cm from the lens. m = v/u = (−10)/(−30) = +1/3 ≈ 0.33. The image is virtual, erect and diminished.

or.q: An object is placed 15 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the position, nature and magnification of the image.
or.answer: u = −15 cm, f = +10 cm. 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so v = +30 cm (on the other side of the lens). m = v/u = 30/(−15) = −2. The image is real, inverted and magnified (twice the size).

subparts.q: Draw a ray diagram to show the image formed by a convex lens when the object is placed between F_{1} and 2F_{1}. State the position and nature of the image.
subparts.answer: Diagram: one ray parallel to the principal axis passes through F_{2} after refraction, and one ray through the optical centre goes straight without deviation. They meet beyond 2F_{2}. Image: beyond 2F_{2}; real, inverted and enlarged.

subparts.q: Define 1 dioptre. Find the power of a concave lens of focal length 2 m.
subparts.answer: 1 dioptre is the power of a lens whose focal length is 1 metre. P = 1/f = 1/(−2 m) = −0.5 D.

or.q:
(a) Give two uses each of concave and convex mirrors. [2]
(b) An object 5 cm in length is held 25 cm away from a converging lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the position, size and nature of the image. [3]
or.answer: (a) Concave: torches and vehicle headlights (parallel beams), shaving mirrors, dentists' mirrors, solar furnaces. Convex: rear-view mirrors in vehicles, mirrors at blind turns, security mirrors in shops. (b) u = −25 cm, f = +10 cm. 1/v = 1/10 − 1/25 = 3/50, so v = +16.7 cm. m = v/u = 16.7/(−25) ≈ −0.67, so h′ ≈ −3.3 cm. The image is real, inverted and diminished, 16.7 cm on the other side of the lens.

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: The refractive index of a medium tells us how much light slows down in it compared with a vacuum. Some values are: water 1.33, kerosene 1.44, crown glass 1.52 and diamond 2.42.

subparts.q: In which of these four media does light travel fastest?
subparts.answer: Water, which has the lowest refractive index.

subparts.q: Which of these is optically the densest?
Calculate the speed of light in diamond. (Speed of light in vacuum = 3 × 10^{8} m/s.)
